title: Time zones, durations, business days and cron
purpose: Date arithmetic on the time zone data Node already ships: convert a time between zones, read or write an ISO 8601 duration, add or count business days, and list a cron schedule's next run times.
inputs: ISO 8601 times (`2026-03-08T02:30`, an instant with `Z` or an offset, `@` epoch seconds, or `now`) and IANA zone names. Business days take holidays as `--holiday` dates or a `--holidays` file. Cron reads standard five-field, Quartz and Jenkins `H` expressions, with `--job` for `H`.
examples: toil util time convert 2026-03-08T02:30 --zone America/New_York --to Europe/London
toil util time business-days diff 2026-12-24T15:00 2026-12-29T10:00 --zone America/Chicago
toil util time cron 'H H(0-7) * * 1-5' --dialect jenkins --job platform/api-build
verifies: Each answer is checked a second way: a conversion is read back as the same instant, a duration's canonical text as the same parts, business days are counted again day by day, and each cron run is matched against every field of the expression.
limits: A clock time that a daylight saving change skipped or showed twice is always pointed out, never quietly picked. No country's holidays are built in. Years and months have no fixed length, so a duration with them has no total in seconds.
